status_reason: Target (coating thickness), product (tablets) and location (pan coater) are stated, but no spectra, reference data or pan-coater evidence are given, so this first assessment rests on other processes.
answer: Coating thickness is a reasonable first test for NIR + Raman: the source reports NIR + Raman as the best combination for pellet coating in a fluidized bed, and reports that combined models predicted coating thickness more accurately than single-method models in that study. A combined probe is not shown to be needed; it matters only if both methods must sample the same spot. Test NIR + Raman against the best single method on the same validation tablets before deciding.

inline.headline: Test NIR + Raman in-line in the pan coater, against the best single method, to follow coating thickness to the end point
inline.probe: NIR reflection probe plus Raman probe (785 nm excitation), as separate synchronised probes first
inline.install: Inside the pan coater at a location the client must confirm; the published example mounted both probes in the tablet press feed frame
inline.fiber: Vis-NIR silica fiber (350-2400 nm), which covers 785 nm Raman excitation; Al/Cu-coated silica fibers avoid polymer-jacket fluorescence for Raman
inline.test_against: NIR reflection alone and Raman alone, on the same validation tablets
inline.not_final_because: The NIR + Raman evidence comes from pellet coating in a fluidized bed and blend potency in a feed frame, not from a pan coater; no client spectra or reference data are given; Raman fluorescence and the NIR band edge above 2400 nm are unchecked.

problems.text: NIR + Raman being the best method is not established for this process. The source supports it for pellet coating in a fluidized bed and blend potency in a tablet press feed frame; in general it is not always possible to predict which method will work, so several methods must be tested.
A combined probe is not proven necessary. Same-spot sampling matters for heterogeneous samples; if the coating is uniform, separate synchronised probes can be tested first.
Raman may be masked by fluorescence. For many organic compounds Raman is overwhelmed by much stronger fluorescence, and the coating formulation is unknown.
The NIR range may be cut at the fiber end. NIR is listed as 780-2500 nm, but the Vis-NIR silica fiber is listed as 350-2400 nm, so the band above 2400 nm needs a fiber check.

methods.why: NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method, and diffuse reflection suits scattering solids and powders, so it fits solid tablets.
Raman is complementary to NIR and needs special probes, and it is the second arm of the test; fluorescence can mask its signal.
ATR fiber probes are described for liquids and elastic solids, and MIR is limited to very thin layers, usually under 50 µm.
Fluorimetry needs a secondary emission from the sample, and most chemicals do not fluoresce; use it only if the coating contains a fluorophore.

questions.q: What reference method gives coating thickness, what thickness range and end-point accuracy do you need, and how many batches and tablets are available for calibration and validation?
questions.why: Model building needs a reference and enough data, and the end-point rule must come from your specification.

questions.q: Is coating thickness uniform across tablets and within a tablet, or must NIR and Raman see the same spot?
questions.why: The answer decides between separate synchronised probes and a combined NIR + Raman probe.

questions.q: What is the coating formulation (polymers, colourants, API), and does it fluoresce under the Raman laser?
questions.why: Fluorescence can mask Raman, and the formulation determines which bands carry the thickness information.

questions.q: Where can probes be mounted in the pan coater (port, window, distance to the spectrometer), and what fiber length is needed?
questions.why: Mounting position and distance set the probe type and the fiber family.

questions.q: Do you have earlier in-line or PAT spectra from this coater for the same product?
questions.why: Existing spectra would allow key spectral features to be selected before a full lab test.

experiment.objective: Decide whether fused NIR + Raman models predict coating thickness better than the best single method on the same validation tablets.
steps: Record NIR reflection and Raman spectra (785 nm excitation) on tablets across the coating run, time-synchronised, using the same tablets for both methods.
Measure coating thickness on the same tablets by independent laboratory analysis, not by the instrument's own calibration.
Build NIR-only, Raman-only and low-level fused NIR + Raman PLS models on a calibration set.
Validate all three models on a separate validation set with the same data for each.
Keep a combined probe only if same-spot sampling is needed, and keep the fused model only if it beats the best single method on the validation data.
references: De Man, A, et al. (2024). Evaluating the improvement of blend potency measurements in the feed frame of a rotary tablet press using combined NIR and Raman spectroscopy. Analytical Chemistry, 96(26), 10586-10593.
experiment.go_no_go: Client-defined end-point accuracy and thickness range; the criteria come from the client.

pathway.key_features: No spectra were supplied; key features are to be selected from lab spectra by multivariate analysis. Raman is read as shift in cm-1 at 785 nm excitation.
pathway.path_reason: The lab test and key-feature selection come first; Path A, the chemometric model, is the likely later step if the test succeeds.

multispectral.why: NIR sees hydrogen bonds and polar groups while Raman sees the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, so their information is complementary.
multispectral.test: Build NIR-only, Raman-only and fused NIR + Raman PLS models on the same calibration and validation tablets; keep the fused model only if it predicts coating thickness better than the best single method. Move to a combined NIR + Raman probe only if the same-spot check fails.

assumptions: The coating thickness target is one layer thickness per tablet; the client has not stated the range.
The pan coater can take a probe port or window; this is not confirmed.
The tablets are solid and scatter light, so NIR reflection is the first interface to test.
